headline: A Compromised CA Breaks the Chain of Trust
lede: An intermediate certificate authority has been compromised, putting its inherited TLS trust at risk. Revoke affected certificates, rotate keys, and check whether your software has received the relevant deny-list and trust-store updates.

headline: 3.7 Million Polygons, Triangulated in 489 Milliseconds
lede: GLOBUS’s earstrip turns sprawling map geometry into GPU-ready triangles with an optimized C++ and WebAssembly pipeline. The library keeps difficult polygons in view while shaving time from a familiar rendering bottleneck.

headline: A Small Model Pretends to Be a Terminal
lede: WorldTUI trains a 360-million-parameter model to predict terminal screens from keystrokes, without running a real shell or filesystem. It is compact, local, and entertaining—and still loses the plot when unfamiliar commands arrive.

headline: A New Assault on Integer Multiplication
lede: A proposed construction aims to improve the long-standing O(n log n) multiplication bound by amplifying a small FFT saving through tensor products. The idea is plausible but not yet fully verified, with data movement and generalization still requiring careful proof.

headline: Reasoning Without the Language Model
lede: Minotaur replaces text prediction with networks of drives, constraints, and explicit relations. Its promise is certifiable deduction without an LLM; its present weakness is the gap between an ambitious account and an inspectable, working demonstration.
pullquote: Explicit structure is only as persuasive as the evidence that lets us inspect it.

headline: Railway Tells Customers to Rotate Their Secrets
lede: Railway says an unauthorized party may have accessed encrypted environment variables—and, in some cases, their decrypted contents. Deployments paused while customers rotated credentials, checked logs, and waited for clearer answers about exposure.

headline: Claude Duet Works Between Your Prompts
lede: Anthropic’s research-preview agent monitors calendars and inboxes, prepares briefs, drafts documents, and handles approved tasks from a cloud computer. It is a move from conversational assistance toward delegated work, with usage limits and judgment errors still part of the specification.

headline: Apple Finally Removes the Extra Icons
lede: Apple is reversing macOS Tahoe’s default menu icons in the upcoming Golden Gate release. The retreat is a useful design lesson: decoration earns its place only when it improves recognition, scanning, or access to an action.

headline: A PyPI Release Arrives With a Credential Stealer
lede: LiteLLM 1.107.0 was poisoned across platform wheels and related container tags, using startup hooks to harvest credentials and a backdoor to fetch more code. Anyone who installed the release should treat the host as compromised, rotate secrets, and investigate the published indicators.

headline: Google Sets Its Rust Rules at Scale
lede: Google’s Rust Style Guide turns ecosystem conventions into operating rules for large, distributed codebases. Ownership, APIs, errors, unsafe code, concurrency, and crate structure all get the same treatment: make future refactoring cheaper and intent easier to read.
